newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends higher recovering from correction.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends higher recovering from correction.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended higher Friday, recovering from a short-lived correction it suffered this week as persistent low inventories drove the market up, buoying crude and gasoline as well.

"The fact is we are still in a bull market where fundamentals are strong. Heating oil tends to go through these fairly shallow corrections in the scope of its steep gains made since July," said Bob McMinn, president of MPAS Inc, a petroleum consulting firm based in Toronto.
November heating oil settled 1.23 cents a gallon higher at 71.72 cents.
News heat inventories were being replenished after hitting record lows ingnited a bout of profit-taking earlier this week after prices had risen more than 30 percent since July.
However, the American Petroleum Institute said heating oil stocks remained a low 14.8 million barrels below a year ago as of October 18.
Crude followed heat up, with December crude settling 35 cents up at $24.86 a barrel.
November gasoline ended the day up 0.88 cent at 70.10 cents a gallon, rebounding from early session losses as the rally in heat sharpened.
November gasoline rose as high as 70.20 cents, a contract high and gasoline's highest price since May 6.
The intraday declines in gasoline were temporary, analysts said, because a push to increase heating oil stocks is shifting refinery ouput away from gasoline production, cutting into gasoline supply.
"We are cannibalizing gasoline stocks to make distillate," said MPAS's McMinn.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
